fuente.nota: Text shortened by paragraphs; sentences unchanged.

parrafos: A hospital is a place where a person goes to be healed when they are sick or injured. The difference between a hospital and other healthcare places like a clinic or a doctor's office is that a hospital will have beds where patients can stay overnight. These patients are called inpatients. The goal of inpatient treatment is to provide 24-7 medical stabilization, which is why this type of treatment has more of a hospital-like feel since patients are monitored by doctors, nurses, therapists, and social workers. Treatment is structured and has a schedule that can include individual therapy, group therapy, case management, and support groups.
Hospitals also treat people who do not stay overnight, called outpatients. Doctors and nurses work at hospitals. Doctors make use of advanced medical technology to heal patients.

Patients who are staying at the hospital will always be under the care of doctors and nurses who are always available for taking care of the injured or sick patients. Hospitals always have the tools and machines needed for treating the patients.

The word hospital originally meant "a place where people can stay". There have been hospitals for sick people since ancient times. They were often created and run by religious groups. In the early modern period, hospitals began to be funded by donations from rich people and by governments. Today, hospitals might get money from the government, from charging patients for treatments and check-ups, from patients' health insurance, from people giving to charity or a mixture of those things.
resumen_es: Defines what a hospital is and how it differs from other healthcare centres, explains the difference between inpatients and outpatients, and reviews its origins and sources of funding.
nivel_motivo: The lexical level is raised by a few medical terms (inpatient, stabilization), but the text is short, with simple syntax and an everyday topic, typical of B1.

ideas_clave.idea: Unlike clinics or surgeries, hospitals have beds so that sick or injured people can be admitted and stay overnight.
Inpatient care aims to stabilise patients round the clock under the supervision of a multidisciplinary team, following a structured programme of therapies.
Hospitals also treat people who go home the same day, and they always have staff and equipment available to care for patients.
Originally meaning a place to stay, hospitals have existed since antiquity, first run by religious bodies and later financed by wealthy donors and governments.
Nowadays they are funded by public money, patient fees, insurance, charity or a combination of these sources.

resumen_modelo: The text explains what a hospital is and how it operates. What distinguishes it from a clinic or a doctor's surgery is that it provides beds, allowing patients to be admitted overnight. These inpatients receive continuous care from doctors, nurses and other professionals, following a structured treatment schedule, while outpatients are treated without staying. Hospitals also rely on advanced technology and permanently available staff. Historically, they date back to ancient times, when they were usually run by religious groups; later, rich benefactors and governments funded them. Today, their income may come from the state, patient fees, insurance or charity.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, what distinguishes a hospital from a clinic or a doctor's office?
opciones: It has beds where patients can stay overnight
It is always run by the government
It employs nurses as well as doctors
respuestas: It has beds where patients can stay overnight
preguntas.cita: a hospital will have beds where patients can stay overnight
preguntas.explicacion: The difference the text points out is having beds for patients to stay overnight. It does not say that a hospital only treats serious injuries or that it is always public, and nurses are not an exclusive feature.

preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals have existed since ancient times; in the early modern period, what changed was their funding (donations from the rich and from governments).

respuestas: In the past they were mostly created and run by religious groups; in the early modern period they began to receive donations from the rich and money from governments; today they may combine public funds, patient charges, health insurance and charity.
